rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “sign” means an extraordinary sign: a wonder or miracle.
rows.anchor: burada “âyet” alâmet-i acîbe yani hârika ve mucize mânasınadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite noun in a conditional context has generic force, so “a sign” means any sign.
rows.anchor: siyâk-ı şartta nekre, siyâk-ı nefiyde gibi âm olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will not learn or consider the outcome before it arrives; they turn from every sign and dismiss it as magic.
rows.anchor: ibret almak istemiyorlar da her gördükleri âyetten yüz çeviriyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the indefinite sign is generic here, they disregard every sign, proof, and miracle.
rows.anchor: her türlü âyete şâmildir. Yani hiçbir âyeti, hiçbir delîli, hiçbir mucizeyi nazar-ı itibara almıyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One established sense of “mustamir” is something recurrent, continuously and regularly proceeding.
rows.anchor: Birisi mâruf olduğu üzere yeniden yeniye muttariden cârî ve mütevâlî demektir.

rows.speaker: Buhârî
rows.claim: Bukhari transmits the sense “passing” or “transient” for mustamir.
rows.anchor: geçici, yani gelip geçici demektir ki Buhârî’de bu mâna menkuldür.

rows.speaker: Ebu’l- Âliye ve Dahhâk
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya and Dahhak transmit a sense of firm or strong, derived from mirrah, meaning strength.
rows.anchor: kuvvet mânasına “mirre”den müştak olarak muhkem demek olduğu Ebu’l- Âliye ve Dahhâk’tan nakledilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transient sense suits magic, while the strong, continuing sense suits the succession of signs and miracles; each sense has a fitting application.
rows.anchor: Sihir tâbirine yakışan gelip geçici mânasına olmaktır. Âyât ve mu‘cizâtın tevâlî ve te‘âkubuna yakışan da kuvvetli ve mütemâdî mânasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after seeing the moon split, they called it the magic of Abu Kabsha’s son, waited for travelers, then called it magic again when travelers confirmed it.
rows.anchor: bakalım etraftan gelecek yolculara soralım” dediler, gelenler de gördüklerini söyleyince

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since magic is false, calling it powerful or regular magic exposes their bewilderment and a kind of contradiction.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki sihir, her ne de olsa bâtıl olacağından böyle demeleri şaşkınlıkla bir nevi tenakuza düşmüş olduklarını iş‘âr eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rejected the Prophet, his reports, and the signs and miracles he showed, calling them lies.
rows.anchor: Ve tekzib ettiler Peygamber’i ve getirdiği haberleri ve gösterdiği âyetleri ve mucizeleri yalana nisbet edip inkâr eylediler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial rested on their desires and inclinations, not knowledge, evidence, or regard for what truth required.
rows.anchor: bir şey bildiklerinden, bir delîle istinad ettiklerinden değil de {وَٱتَّبَعُوٓا۟ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ} hevâlarına uydular keyiflerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every matter is settled in God’s knowledge and decree and proceeds toward its appointed course.
rows.anchor: Her işi Allah teâlâ’nın ilm ü takdîrinde kararını almış, ona doğru gitmektedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every matter has an end at which its truth becomes clear; in time the Prophet’s true worth and the nature and ill consequences of their desires will be manifest.
rows.anchor: Hepsinin varıp karar kılacağı bir gaye ve âkıbet vardır ki hakikati o zaman tebeyyün eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The important reports may concern the circumstances of past peoples or matters of the afterlife, including reports in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Yani geçen ümmetlerin ahvâline veya âhirete müte‘allik haberlerden Kur’an’da öyle mühim haberler de geldi ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports contain deterrent threats, admonitions, or painful outcomes from which people must take warning.
rows.anchor: onda zecredecek, vazgeçirecek tehdit, sakındıracak öğüt, yahut sakınılması lâzım gelen acı âkıbetler var.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muzdajer can be a verbal noun with mīm or a noun of place.
rows.anchor: “Müzdecer” masdar-ı mîmî de ism-i mekân da olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Consummate wisdom” is wisdom that reaches the highest degree of sound construction and attainment of its goal.
rows.anchor: “Hikmet-i Bâliğa” ihkâmın ve gayeye isabetin en yüksek derecesine ermiş hikmet demek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Consummate wisdom” may be an appositive to “that” or muzdaǧar, or the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: “mâ”dan veya “müzdecer”den bedel, yahut mahzuf bir mübtedânın haberidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that the Qur’an came with rebukes and reports that constitute consummate wisdom.
rows.anchor: Yani bir hikmet-i bâliğa olan zecirler ve haberlerle Kur’an geldi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the whole course of events as it unfolds is itself consummate wisdom.
rows.anchor: bunların hepsi, cereyân-ı hâlin böyle olması bir hikmet-i bâliğadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warnings bring no benefit to them.
rows.anchor: Demek ki o inzarlar fâide vermiyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to turn from the disbelievers who follow their desires rather than waste time arguing, and attend to the approaching Hour.
rows.anchor: o hâlde sen de onlardan -o hevâları peşinde giden münkirlerden- yüz çevir boş yere mücadele ile uğraşma da yaklaşmakta olan Sâ‘at’e bak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller’s day explains the Hour just mentioned as approaching.
rows.anchor: gün yaklaşmakta olduğu zikrolunan Sâ‘at’i bir beyandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day” could attach to an implied mention, but the author finds its attachment to “they emerge” more fitting.
rows.anchor: Bu “yevm” mukadder zikre müte‘allik olabilirse de aşağıdaki يَخْرُجُونَ’a müte‘allik olması daha muvâfıktır.

rows.speaker: tecviz edenler
rows.claim: Some interpreters allow “turn away from them” to attach to the Resurrection Day, taking it to mean refraining from interceding for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A required waqf after “from them” rules out that attachment.

rows.speaker: Kavl-i meşhur
rows.claim: The well-known view identifies the caller as Israfil.

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Ebussuud allows the call to be like the divine “Be, and it is” command, in which case God is the caller.

rows.speaker: author

rows.claim: The caller summons them to reckoning, to the gathering, or to resurrection for the gathering.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes are humbled and downcast in fear and awe at the terror of the scene.

rows.claim: The disbelievers call it a difficult day, implying that it will not be so for the believers.
